newsitem.title: USA: Suspect laundering money -- in N.Y. laundries.
newsitem.headline: Suspect laundering money -- in N.Y. laundries.

text.p: New York police are looking for a suspect who truly does launder money.
An unknown man has been feeding counterfeit five- and ten-dollar bills into money-changing machines at coin-operated laundries, police in Suffolk County, N.Y., said Thursday.
He has hit at least four laundries in suburban Long Island east of New York City, police said.
In one instance, he fed 70 phony ten-dollar bills into a change machine, getting 140 real five-dollar bills in exchange, police said.
Although the culprit remains at large, he has been captured on a video surveillance camera and police said they have a detailed description.
Police say they do not have a total on how much counterfeit money the suspect has exchanged for real bills. They are offering a $1,000 reward, in real bills, in the case.
